# MSBuild Code Review — `StyleIssues.sln`

**Scope**: 2 `.csproj`, 2 `.fsproj`, 2 `Directory.Build.props`, 2 `Directory.Build.targets`, 1 `.sln` — 9 files total.

---

## 🔴 Errors (will cause build failures or incorrect behavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props`, line 10 — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

For single-targeting projects (all projects here target only `net8.0`), the SDK sets `$(TargetFramework)` in its own `.props` import *after* `Directory.Build.props` has already been evaluated. At the point this condition runs, `$(TargetFramework)` is still **empty**, so the condition is **always false** and `GenerateDocumentationFile` is never set.

**Fix**: Move this block to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is imported *after* the SDK props and the project body, where `$(TargetFramework)` is reliably populated:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–10 — Property defaults in `.targets` override project-level settings

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

`.targets` files are imported **after** the project body. MSBuild uses last-write-wins for properties, so these unconditional assignments **silently override** any value set in an individual `.csproj`. This directly breaks `LibB/LibB.csproj` (line 13), which tries to set `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` but is overridden back to `true`.

**Fix**: Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This lets projects opt out by setting the property before the condition is checked.

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13 — Unquoted `Condition` on `$(Configuration)`

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

The condition value is **not quoted**. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during evaluation in certain IDE contexts or `dotnet restore` without `/p:Configuration=…`), this evaluates as ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression that can produce unpredictable behavior. Additionally, `Debug` also needs to be quoted.

**Fix**:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14 — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

This replaces the SDK-provided constants (`DEBUG`, `TRACE`) instead of appending to them. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop compiling in.

**Fix**:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45 — Publish-on-build re-invokes the project, causing double-build and file races

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

This re-enters the **same project** via the `<MSBuild>` task with a new global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), which creates a **second evaluation instance**. Both instances share the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, causing file-write races that can produce corrupt outputs or intermittent failures — especially under parallel builds (`-m`).

**Fix**: Remove the re-entrant `<MSBuild>` call. Instead, hook Publish into the normal build pipeline:

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild"
        AfterTargets="Build"
        DependsOnTargets="Publish"
        Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true' and '$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'" />
```

---

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–8 — F# compile order is wrong

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />

```xml

</Target>
```

Without `Inputs`/`Outputs`, this target runs on **every build** regardless of whether anything changed, breaking incremental build performance. Additionally, the version `1.0.0` is hardcoded rather than sourced from a property.

**Fix** (if the target is needed at all):
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Outputs="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version $(Version)" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker" AlwaysCreate="true" />
</Target>
```
